evidence_quotes.quote: We conducted weekly smartphone surveys in over 300 households across informal settlements.
A weekly survey capturing the access and barriers to sanitation and water (for drinking, cooking, sanitation and washing).
The monthly WASH survey reports if a complaint was registered, and if was dealt with over the last month.
This work took place under the ‘Scaling-up Off-grid Sanitation’ project (SOS; ES/T007877/1), and we outline below the methods used to collect the smartphone survey work package of this project.
The aim was for each country to have a paired list of 50 CBS users and 50 CBS non-users, with an even gender balance with a total sample of 300 across all countries.

criterion_notes.c1: The subject domain of the survey and deposited dataset is household off-grid sanitation (specifically container-based sanitation, CBS, contrasted with other sanitation types) and household water access in urban informal settlements.
criterion_notes.c2: Fails under BOTH the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading. Under the plain wording, although the Background notes that the parent project ('Scaling-up Off-grid Sanitation') aims to explore management and regulation of off-grid sanitation and Section 3 lists deposited dataset files containing questions on elections (SOS_Elections.xlsx) and monthly WASH complaints (SOS_WASH Monthly.xlsx), this Data in Brief article only describes survey deployment, compensation points, and data-cleaning protocols without examining any legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, no rule-type mechanism governing service access (eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation/tenure rules, tariffs/cost recovery, discretion, enforcement, or regulatory/ownership structure) is examined. Both readings lead to exclusion.
criterion_notes.c3: This is a Data in Brief 'Data Article' (dataset descriptor) documenting 16 deposited Excel files, ODK forms, micro-task point compensation calculators, and R/Python data-cleaning scripts. Beyond operational survey response and attrition rates (Table 2), it presents no empirical analysis or substantive empirical evidence.
criterion_notes.c4: No outcome on water or sanitation access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion is reported in the article; only operational smartphone survey response rates and attrition rates are reported (Table 2).
criterion_notes.c5: While the target population, final sample sizes (109 in Kenya, 98 in Peru, 103 in South Africa), and smartphone survey protocol are described, no analytical governance exposure or reported service-access outcome is present because the publication is solely a dataset descriptor.
criterion_notes.c6: The full text is written in English.

study_design: Dataset descriptor / Data Article documenting a 12-month longitudinal high-frequency smartphone survey
country: Kenya, Peru, and South Africa (pilot only in Haiti)
population_and_sample: 310 adult respondents (109 in Nairobi, Kenya; 98 in Lima, Peru; 103 in Cape Town, South Africa) across households in informal settlements, sampled as paired container-based sanitation (CBS) users and non-users
rationale: Excluded (E12 - Wrong study design; also fails c2, c3, c4, and c5). This publication is a Data in Brief 'Data Article' (dataset descriptor) that documents the ODK smartphone survey architecture, participant micro-payment compensation scheme, sampling protocol, and data-cleaning rules for 16 deposited Excel files from the 'Scaling-up Off-grid Sanitation' project in Kenya, Peru, and South Africa. It conducts no empirical analysis, examines no legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance mechanism (under either the plain wording or the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2), and reports no water or sanitation service-access outcomes (reporting only operational survey response and attrition rates in Table 2).
